title: Optimal Duration of Urinary Catheterization After Right-Sided Colectomy
official: Optimal Duration of Urinary Catheterization After Right-Sided Colectomy: Prospective, Randomized, Non-inferiority Trial
summary:
The goal of this prospective, randomized trial is to determine the optimal duration of urinary catheterization in patients that receive elective, right-sided colectomy. The main objectives of this study are:

* To compare rates of urinary retention in patients with post operative urinary catheter duration of 0 days and 1 day following right-sided colectomy.
* To compare rates of urinary tract infection (UTI) in patients with postoperative urinary catheter duration of 0 days and 1 day following right-sided colectomy.

Enrolled participants will be randomized to one of two groups, immediate removal of urinary catheter at the conclusion of the operation or removal of urinary catheter on post operative day one.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older.
* Scheduled for elective ileocecectomy, right hemicolectomy, or extended right hemicolectomy using an open, laparoscopic, or robotic approach.
* American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status class I-III.
* Ability and willingness to provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of urinary tract malignancy.
* Emergent or urgent surgery.
* Right hemicolectomy performed with another major surgical procedure on the same day.
* Genitourinary tract injury during surgery that precludes participation.
* History of urinary retention following a previous procedure, surgery, or urinary catheter removal.
* History of urinary retention that is not being actively treated.
* Neurogenic bladder.
* Chronic indwelling Foley catheter or suprapubic catheter.
* History of cystectomy or a surgically created urinary conduit, including a neobladder or ileal conduit.
* Chronic kidney disease greater than stage 2.
* History of chronic urinary tract infection.
* Current extravesicular or enterourethral fistula.
* Perioperative epidural catheter placement.
* Incarceration.
* Inability or unwillingness to provide informed consent.
* Pregnancy.
